headline: Chips Carry the Tape as Water Names Split Violently
body_html:
Stocks leaned higher at midday Tuesday, with 304 of the 544 names we track rising and 235 falling. Prices are not final. Semiconductors led every group, gaining an average of 3.39%, and materials followed with a 1.75% advance. Industrials added 0.55%, while software slipped 0.31%.

Chips are the dominant theme. MaxLinear is up 9.63% and Alpha and Omega Semiconductor has gained 8.94%. That fits a market strategist's view that the AI trade is approaching a now-or-never moment to rebound. The standout action is in water. Pentair leads the universe, up 11.64%, while rival Xylem is down 11.03%, the steepest drop we track. Hawkins, a specialty chemicals name, is up 10.16%.

Into the close, watch whether the chip leadership holds and whether software stabilizes. Oil also matters. Futures were firmer as crude pulled back ahead of a Fed decision, but a Houthi claim of a missile strike on a Saudi refinery keeps energy headlines live. Valero is down 7.66%. Wednesday, October 28, is the next trading day.

briefs.headline: Water stocks pull in opposite directions
briefs.body: Pentair is up 11.64% and Xylem is down 11.03%, an unusually sharp split inside one corner of industrials. Investors appear to be sorting winners from losers rather than trading the theme as a group. Both moves are intraday and could change by the close.

briefs.headline: Smaller chipmakers lead the rally
briefs.body: MaxLinear has gained 9.63% and Alpha and Omega Semiconductor 8.94%, helping lift the semiconductor group by an average of 3.39%. A strategist's note that the AI trade faces a pivotal stretch adds context. The test is whether buyers stay in late in the session.

briefs.headline: Refinery claim keeps oil in focus
briefs.body: Yemen's Houthis say they struck a Saudi refinery with a missile. Even so, futures pointed higher as crude eased, and the energy group is little changed, down 0.04%. Valero is the notable laggard, off 7.66% in refining.

briefs.headline: Forecasters see inflation lingering into next year
briefs.body: A Reuters poll of economists points to stubbornly high global inflation continuing into next year. That backdrop frames the Fed decision traders are bracing for. It also helps explain a market that is rewarding selective leadership more than broad risk-taking.

briefs.headline: Industrial winners and losers diverge
briefs.body: Lincoln Electric is up 8.69%, while UniFirst is down 8.00% and Armstrong World Industries has fallen 7.77%. Applied Industrial Technologies is off 5.87%. The sector average is a modest 0.55% gain, which hides a wide range of individual outcomes.

briefs.headline: Britain's borrowing costs draw attention before budget
briefs.body: The UK sold five-year debt at its highest cost since 2008, ahead of a budget statement. The move underlines how sensitive bond buyers remain to fiscal plans and inflation risk. It is a reminder that rate pressure is not confined to the US.
